expectations.name: 01-page-written
expectations.text:
docs/philosophy.md is written or changed: a rule that guides many decisions is a tenet, which the map gives the
philosophy page.

expectations.name: 02-structure
expectations.text:
Each page the agent wrote or changed meets the map's structural rules: a declared kind, listed in its guide, links
and anchors that resolve, the kind's sections in order, a record named NNNN-<slug>.md, no rejected synonym.

expectations.name: 03-lead
expectations.text: The philosophy page opens with a lead under its title, not a restatement of the title.

expectations.name: 04-reason-told
expectations.text:
The page states the tenet, what it rules out, and why, told as it happened: the Redis queue that lost receipt jobs
and only one volunteer could restore, not only a conclusion such as "fewer services are simpler".
expectations.evidence: The tenet 'Add a service we operate only when Postgres cannot do the job and two volunteers can restore it' is followed by the narrated history: 'In 2023 Redis was rejected for sessions because only one volunteer would have run it. Redis was later used for Celery, but in March 2025 it evicted 300 receipt jobs; only one volunteer could restore it.' The page also states what it rules out: 'This rules out adding a service for a job Postgres can already handle, or leaving recovery dependent on one volunteer. External services remain an option: larder uses a card gateway, and a hosted service that no volunteer has to operate is acceptable.'

expectations.name: 05-fact-stated
expectations.text: The tenet links the two records that apply it: sessions in the database and background jobs on Postgres.
expectations.evidence: match /adr/0001-.*adr/0002-|adr/0002-.*adr/0001-/ in ['docs/philosophy.md']: {'docs/philosophy.md': 'adr/0001-keep-sessions-in-the-database.md) and\n[run background jobs on Postgres](adr/0002-'}

expectations.name: 06-trap
expectations.text:
No decision record is added: the map gives a rule that guides many decisions to the philosophy page, and one decision
applying it to a record.
